subject: Re: Northwind case study — claims + proof review (v5)
body:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Wallace <ethan_wallace@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Simran Kaur <simran_kaur@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Oct 18, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Northwind case study — claims + proof review (v5)
Attachments: Northwind_case_study_draft_v5.docx; metrics_proof_sheet_northwind_v3.xlsx; Messaging_Pillars_Approved_Claims_v2.pdf

Team —

Attaching draft v5 + the proof sheet I have so far. Can you please do a claims + proof pass today so we can keep the Northwind publish window intact?

Specific items to validate:
1) Performance economics claim language (p95 latency + $/1M tokens). We need to ensure we’re using approved phrasing + the proof sheet matches.
2) Reliability/fallback claim: we currently say “automatic fallback during capacity constraints” — need to confirm the actual routing policy Northwind uses and what we can state publicly.
3) Dedicated sizing: we reference “reserved capacity” and “burst” in the solution section — please confirm accuracy.
4) Any “too strong” phrases (e.g., “zero downtime,” “guaranteed,” etc.).

If you can reply with line-level comments or bullet notes (what to change + why + source), I’ll consolidate with Ethan.

Thanks,
Soojin

—

From: Ethan Wallace <ethan_wallace@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Simran Kaur <simran_kaur@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Oct 18, 2025 at 9:34 AM
Subject: Re: Northwind case study — claims + proof review (v5)

+1 on avoiding overly absolute statements.

Also flagging a couple spots where I used numbers as placeholders because we were still waiting on the final “publishable” ranges:
- “~35–45% lower p95 latency”
- “~25–35% lower $/1M tokens”

If we don’t get comfort on exact figures, I can rewrite those to qualitative + add methodology language (“based on Northwind’s production traffic, measured over X weeks…”). Just need your call on how strict we want to be with metrics this first story.

Ethan

—

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Wallace <ethan_wallace@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Simran Kaur <simran_kaur@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Oct 18, 2025 at 10:21 AM
Subject: Re: Northwind case study — claims + proof review (v5)

Reviewed v5. Notes below (mostly tightening technical accuracy / claim strength):

1) Reliability language
- Current draft: “Zero downtime during the migration.”
  - Change to: “No customer-visible downtime during cutover (per Northwind’s incident log for the migration window).”
  - Reason: We can’t assert “zero downtime” globally. Also makes it clear it’s scoped.

- Current draft: “Automatic fallback to a compatible model if capacity is constrained.”
  - This is true, but we should specify it’s a policy they configured (not magic). Suggest:
    - “Configured routing + fallback policies to keep the assistant online during capacity or regional constraints.”

2) Dedicated sizing / burst
- The phrase “burst capacity” is a bit loaded. Northwind’s setup is reserved pool + overflow to a secondary reserved pool in another region (not on-demand burst). Recommend:
  - Replace “burst” with “overflow capacity” and avoid implying spot/on-demand.

3) Metrics
- The proof sheet has p95 latency improvement tied to a “before” baseline that includes a period with a transient spike (see SUP-3812). We should not publish a single point estimate unless we can defend the window.
- Suggest publishing ranges + stating the measurement window (“4-week period after rollout vs 4-week pre-rollout excluding incident window”).

4) Console / Optimize statements
- Draft says “Optimize automatically reduced cost.” This reads like we flipped a switch.
  - Better: “Redwood Optimize recommendations helped the team tune batching + caching to reduce unit cost while meeting latency targets.”

If helpful I can add a short technical footnote on how the fallback policy works (region priority + model variant + max queue time).

Markus

—

From: Simran Kaur <simran_kaur@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Wallace <ethan_wallace@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Oct 18, 2025 at 11:06 AM
Subject: Re: Northwind case study — claims + proof review (v5)

+1 to Markus’s points.

On the routing/fallback specifics (what we can safely say):
- They have a primary route pinned to the main model version in us-west.
- Fallback #1: same model family, quantized variant, same region (used when queue time threshold is hit).
- Fallback #2: compatible model version in us-east (used when regional saturation or maintenance).

I would avoid:
- Naming the exact model variants unless Northwind explicitly approves (they were sensitive in the intro call).
- Saying “guaranteed latency” — best to say “met p95 latency target” or “kept p95 within target during peak hours.”

Metrics sourcing:
- p95 latency + throughput should come from Redwood Console dashboards (we can cite “Console” as system-of-record).
- Cost ($/1M tokens) is from their internal billing export + our usage analytics. If we use it publicly, we need the methodology sentence + clear “results vary.”

If you want, I can provide a one-paragraph “how measured” block that matches the proof guide template.

Simran

—

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Wallace <ethan_wallace@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>, Simran Kaur <simran_kaur@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Oct 18, 2025 at 12:18 PM
Subject: Re: Northwind case study — claims + proof review (v5)

Thanks all — this is exactly what we need.

Decision from program side: for Story #1, we should default to ranges + methodology unless the customer explicitly signs off on exact figures (and Legal has no concerns). We can always tighten later.

Soojin — can you update the claims to align with the Messaging Pillars doc (attached) and add the metrics disclaimer language that Legal prefers?

Also: please make sure we’re not implying “burst/on-demand” Dedicated, per Markus’s note.

Camila

—

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Wallace <ethan_wallace@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>, Simran Kaur <simran_kaur@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Oct 18, 2025 at 3:02 PM
Subject: Re: Northwind case study — claims + proof review (v5)

Got it. Proposed edits (please sanity check):

A) Performance economics (replace the current paragraph)
- Replace with: “After moving to Redwood Dedicated and tuning batching + caching based on Redwood Optimize recommendations, Northwind saw materially lower p95 latency and unit cost on production traffic while maintaining response quality.”
- Then add a callout w/ ranges (pending final customer approval):
  - “Observed results (Northwind, production): ~35–45% lower p95 latency; ~25–35% lower cost per 1M tokens.”
- Add methodology sentence: “Measured over a 4-week period after rollout vs a 4-week pre-rollout baseline (excluding an incident window; see SUP-3812).”

B) Reliability / fallback
- Replace “automatic fallback” with: “Configured routing + fallback policies to keep the assistant online during capacity or regional constraints.”
- Remove “zero downtime,” replace with “no customer-visible downtime during cutover (per Northwind’s migration window).”

C) Dedicated language
- Replace “burst capacity” with “overflow capacity” and avoid implying on-demand.

D) Optimize language
- Replace “Optimize automatically reduced cost” with “Optimize recommendations helped the team tune batching + caching…” (per Markus).

E) Proof sources
- Add a small “Data sources” line in the footnote: “Latency/throughput from Redwood Console; cost estimates based on Redwood usage analytics + Northwind’s billing export.”

Ethan — if you’re good with the above, can you implement in v6 and send back to me for one more quick pass? Markus/Simran — can you confirm the fallback description is accurate enough without being too detailed?

Soojin

—

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Wallace <ethan_wallace@redwoodinference.com>, Simran Kaur <simran_kaur@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Oct 18, 2025 at 4:41 PM
Subject: Re: Northwind case study — claims + proof review (v5)

Looks good. The fallback description you proposed is accurate and safely abstracted.

One small tweak: instead of “no customer-visible downtime during cutover (per Northwind’s migration window)” I’d say:
- “No customer-reported downtime during cutover, based on Northwind’s incident log for the migration window.”

That keeps us from making an absolute claim about “visibility,” and ties it to their source.

Otherwise +1 to ranges + methodology. That should keep us consistent with the approved messaging + avoid SUP-3812 foot-guns.

Markus
